docs.summary: The main entry point for the Paper immediate-mode UI system. Manages the frame lifecycle, element hierarchy, rendering, text layout, and input scaling.

members.name: AnimateBool
members.signature: public float AnimateBool(bool target, float duration = 0.2f, Func<float, float>? easing = null, string? id = null, int callerLine = 0)

docs.summary:
Smoothly animates a 0..1 progress value toward 1 when `target` is true and toward 0 when it is false, returning the eased value. State is stored on [`CurrentParent`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Paper~CurrentParent); if that element isn't recreated next frame, the storage is wiped automatically (so the animation resets when the element reappears).

Each call site gets its own slot via `CallerLineNumberAttribute`, so you can stack independent animations on a single element:

```csharp
float hoverT   = gui.AnimateBool(IsHovered, 0.12f, Easing.SineInOut);
float pressedT = gui.AnimateBool(IsActive,  0.06f);
```

If you call `AnimateBool` from inside a loop or a wrapper method that hides the call site, pass an explicit `id` to keep slots distinct.

params.easing: Optional easing applied on read; null = linear. The underlying progress is stored linear, so reversing target produces a smooth reversal regardless of easing shape.
params.id: Optional explicit slot id for use inside loops or wrapper helpers.
params.callerLine: Call site line number, filled in by the compiler.

members.name: AnimateFloat
members.signature: public float AnimateFloat(float target, float speed = 8f, string? id = null, int callerLine = 0)

docs.summary: Smoothly chases a continuously-changing numeric `target` using frame-rate- independent exponential smoothing. Returns the current interpolated value. Higher `speed` = faster catch-up (8 = ~99% within 0.5s). State is stored on [`CurrentParent`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Paper~CurrentParent).
docs.remarks: Use for values that change every frame (cursor position, scroll offset, animated number readouts). For binary on/off transitions prefer [`AnimateBool`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Paper~AnimateBool).

members.name: AnimateSpring
members.signature: public float AnimateSpring(float target, float frequency = 6f, float damping = 0.7f, string? id = null, int callerLine = 0)

docs.summary: Spring-based chase toward `target`. Maintains both position and velocity, so rapid target changes produce natural overshoot and settling. Returns the current position.

params.frequency: Oscillation frequency in Hz (higher = stiffer / faster response).
params.damping: 0 = undamped (rings forever), 1 = critically damped (no overshoot), values in between produce decaying oscillation.
params.id: Optional explicit slot id for use inside loops or wrapper helpers.
params.callerLine: Call site line number, filled in by the compiler.

docs.summary: One-shot 0..1 ramp: when `trigger` goes from false to true, ramps from 0 to 1 over `duration` seconds and stays at 1 until released. Going false resets to 0. Useful for fire-once flash / pulse / shake effects.
A continuously-cycling oscillator driven by Time that returns a smooth cosine pulse between 0 and 1 for the given period in seconds.

members.name: AnimateAngle

docs.summary: Angle (in degrees) variant of [`AnimateFloat`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Paper~AnimateFloat), taking the shortest path around the circle so animating from 350° to 10° goes the short way (through 360°), not the long way. members.name: Shake
members.signature: public Float2 Shake(bool trigger, float intensity = 4f, float decay = 6f, float frequency = 30f, string? id = null, int callerLine = 0)

docs.summary: Rising-edge shake: when `trigger` goes from false to true, kicks an internal amplitude to 1 which then decays exponentially. Returns a 2-D offset suitable for adding to a translate / position. Apply repeatedly each frame on the same element to drive the shake.

params.decay: Higher = shake fades faster (units of 1/sec; 6 ≈ ~0.5s tail).
params.frequency: How fast the shake oscillates (Hz-ish; 30 = quick chatter).
params.id: Optional explicit slot id for use inside loops or wrapper helpers.
params.callerLine: Call site line number, filled in by the compiler.

docs.summary:
Work out where the pointer should be teleported to keep a [`WrapPointer`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Paper~WrapPointer) drag going, and record the jump. Hosts call this each frame and, when it returns true, move the real cursor to `wrapped`.

Centralised here so every backend wraps identically; a host only has to know how to set the OS cursor position.

params.wrapped: Position to teleport to; equals `pos` when false.
params.margin: How far inside the edge to land, so the pointer does not immediately re-wrap on the following frame.
